keyRules: Maximum height depends on the RPA class: Micro (≤250 g) → 100 ft (~30 m); Light (251 g–25 kg) → 400 ft (~120 m); Medium (26–150 kg) → 400 ft, but limited to 100 m without a Mode S transponder (AAC standard §9.2, §10.1.1, §11.1.5, §11.1.10).

Every RPA, including the Micro class (≤250 g), must be registered with the AAC (§8.1, §9.1, §15.2 of the standard) — unlike most countries, Panama does not exempt the lightest drones from registration. Registration is done in person in Albrook; check the current fee.
Panama does NOT exempt light recreational drones (≤250 g) from registration — unlike most countries, the AAC standard (§8.1, §9.1) requires registration for all RPA classes, including Micro.

Every RPA operation in Panama requires an operating authorization from the AAC (§8.2, §8.20): submit Form 005 (Solicitud de Permiso de Actividades Aéreas Especiales) at least 5 business days in advance.

Minimum distance of 8 km (5 nautical miles) from airports and aerodromes, the Presidency of the Republic, and prisons (§8.10–8.11 of the AAC standard). The standard also prohibits flying in places that compromise State security, such as embassies, public entities, and banks (§8.11), and the AAC maintains restrictions over police stations, hospitals, and the Ministry of Security (AAC statement of 26/9/2025).
During takeoff and landing, keep at least 30 m horizontally and 10 m vertically from people not involved in the operation (§13.1 of the AAC standard).
You must keep the drone within your direct visual contact at all times (RACP).
Night flights are PROHIBITED without a specific AAC exemption.

Third-party civil liability insurance is MANDATORY for every RPA owner (§8.4 of the AAC standard), regardless of use. Flying over people also requires AAC authorization and the consent of those involved (§8.16).

Prohibited, restricted, or danger areas (see the AAC AIP) require specific authorization from the AAC and from the authority in charge of the area — both are required (§13.1 d of the AAC standard). In the Canal zone, protected areas, and indigenous territories, consult the responsible authority before applying for the flight permit.

Anyone operating an RPA — including recreational and Micro class (≤250 g) — must hold an AAC remote pilot license and a Class 3 medical certificate (§8.3, §9.1, §10.1 of the AAC standard). Commercial use additionally requires a commercial operations authorization (§13.3).
importantNotes: Unlike many countries, Panama tiers the maximum height by RPA class: 100 ft (~30 m) for Micro (≤250 g), 400 ft (~120 m) for Light (251 g–25 kg), and 400 ft for Medium (26–150 kg) — but the latter is limited to 100 m without a Mode S transponder. Check your drone's class before planning your flight altitude.

Tourists: the special permit for foreign RPAs or operators (Form 004) lasts a maximum of 15 days and is NOT granted for recreational activities (§8.22 of the AAC standard). Flying for recreation requires registering the RPA with the AAC (all classes, including Micro ≤250 g, §8.1) and an AAC RPA pilot license (§8.3); a foreign license is only validated if a bilateral agreement exists (§18.17). Check with the AAC before traveling.

PANAMA CANAL — RESTRICTED AREA: according to the AAC AIP (ENR 5), operations over the Gatún, Pedro Miguel, and Miraflores locks, the Gatún and Madden dams, and over any ship transiting the Canal are restricted. Authorization from the AAC and from the authority in charge of the area is required (§13.1 d of the AAC standard).
Casco Antiguo, Cinta Costera, Av. Balboa and Calle 50 and surrounding areas: in addition to AAC authorization, you must notify the Servicio de Protección Institucional (SPI) by letter.

🌳 PROTECTED AREAS (MiAmbiente): in SINAP protected areas, only visitors with a valid license/registration may use drones, in accordance with the applicable procedures and fees (Resolución DM-0173-2026, art. 12). Check with the area's administration before flying.
Unlike most countries, AAC registration must be done in person in Albrook — check the current procedure and requirements before your application.

primaryLinks.description: Building 805, Albrook, ground floor — Documentation Department. Submit a request letter (or send it to correspondencia.aac@aeronautica.gob.pa); the AAC will assign an appointment. Bring the registration form, a copy of your RPA license, ID card, specifications, invoice, insurance policy, and payment receipt. Cost: US$20

fields.disclaimerText: Always check the AAC's official sources before flying. This app is a tool, not a legal authority. Panama applies Norma AAC/DG/DSA/001-2021, with WEIGHT-DEPENDENT maximum altitudes and restricted areas in the Panama Canal zone (AIP ENR 5).
